source.title: Modularity in Transformers: Investigating Neuron Separability & Specialization
source.authors: Nicholas Pochinkov; T. Jones; Mohammed Rashidur Rahman

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies task specialization and neuron-set overlap, but it does not test the claim versions about interpretable neuron jobs, explanation accuracy, or neurons as sufficient circuit units.
record.gate_note: The paper reports task-specific neuron selection, cross-task performance after selective pruning, overlap between selected neuron sets, and correspondence with MoEfication clusters. These concern task specialization, not the claim versions' measures of interpretable jobs or explanation quality. The stated selection proportions (ViT 12.5 ± 6.0%; Mistral 3.4 ± 2.6%) define the selected sets and are not outcome rows. Figure-only values are not transcribed as numbers.
record.test_reason: The study selects task-associated MLP neurons by activation ratios and measures cross-task pruning effects, set overlaps and MoEfication-cluster correspondence in ViT-Base and Mistral 7B. It never counts what share of individual neurons have one interpretable job, never scores neuron explanations, and never builds neuron attribution graphs, so none of V1–V7 is tested. Its mention of neurons possibly representing multiple features is in related work only. Arguably T4/uses_without_test is not apt either, since it does not rely on the claim as a tool; T6 with relation 'discusses' (modularity at the population level) is acceptable.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance: selective pruning and MoEfication reveal some interpretable modularity, overlap among similar tasks, structure partly present at random initialization (cited as weak Lottery Ticket evidence), and clear but incomplete cluster correspondence strongest in early/late layers; limits are MLP-only, few models/tasks, qualitative interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses selective pruning based on dataset activations and balanced k-means clustering of MLP input weights; it does not use neuron explanation generation or held-out activation scoring.
record.method_sensitivity: The pruning target changes from 50% to 80% for ViT, with the authors reporting reduced selectivity at the higher target. Results also vary by dataset and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-ratio-selected neurons for one text subset or image class, when pruned, also reduce accuracy on related tasks (e.g., PubMed Central pruning drops several MMLU medical subjects), sometimes asymmetrically; Code pruning raised Abstract Algebra to 118% of baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-selected MLP neuron sets are partially shared across related tasks, giving population-level but incomplete modularity.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected neuron-set overlap patterns in trained models correlate with those in randomly initialized models, with training shifting overlaps toward intuitive class similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some task-specific neuron structure is present at initialization and refined by training.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-selected neurons concentrate in MoEfication clusters more in trained models, most in early (ViT) or early and late (Mistral) layers, less in middle layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-based neuron clusters track task specialization better near input/output layers than in middle layers.

record.problems: The study reports qualitative interpretations and many plotted outcomes without numerical values in the text. It analyzes only MLP neurons, a limited set of models and tasks, and one random initialization seed. The authors state that the interpretation is qualitative and would benefit from more rigorous statistical analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No separately plotted class-pair or text-subset overlap values were transcribed from Figures 1–6; the paper's text summarizes these patterns qualitatively. The selected-neuron proportions are reported as selection settings, not as outcome measures.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one, two or unexplained jobs.
Per-neuron interpretable-job shares across other models and scale; Mistral 7B and ViT are studied but only at the level of task-selected neuron sets.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Whether interpretable-neuron share rises with tools or architecture.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly linked to 'none'. The 12.5±6.0% and 3.4±2.6% values are selection settings, correctly excluded. Figure 4's caption says 'top 1%' while the text says 3.4% for Mistral, an internal inconsistency worth noting. Study cites Bills et al. 2023 (an original source) only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: The proportion of neuron poles with one or more interpretable jobs, and whether explanations tested on held-out activations succeed.
Shares of interpretable jobs across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Interpretability rates across architectures or tools, including the stated InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Whether attribution graphs built from model neurons explain behavior without a replacement model.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned model; also compared with a randomly initialized model
rows.operation_detail: Selectively pruned MLP neurons associated with a Cifar20 class and measured image-classification accuracy on other classes.

conditions.value: 50% and 80% top1 accuracy for the unlearned class

rows.measure: Relative top1 image-classification accuracy across classes after selective pruning
rows.value: Figure 1 only; text reports relatively high overlap for insects and non-insect invertebrates, and correlated decreases for fish, aquatic mammals, and reptiles. The effects of unlearning A on B and B on A were correlated but not symmetric. Selectivity decreased as the target drop approached 80%.
rows.note: The prose describes the cross-class patterns; numerical values are only in the figure.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Selectively pruned neurons associated with each text subset, targeting a 20% drop in next-token top1 accuracy on that subset.
rows.measure: Change in top1 accuracy on other text subsets and MMLU subjects
rows.baseline: Baseline accuracy; relative drops shown in Figure 2
rows.value: Figure 2 only; the text reports significant drops on MMLU professional medicine, Medical Genetics, Clinical Knowledge, Anatomy, College Biology, and College Chemistry.
rows.note: The paper describes these outcomes but does not give their numerical values in the prose.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned model, compared with a randomly initialized model
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap between neuron sets selected as important for different Cifar20 classes.
rows.measure: Intersection of selected neuron sets, divided by the size of one selected set
rows.value: Figure 3 only; the text says trained-model selections had relatively distinct activations compared with random selections. From random to pretrained, overlaps shifted toward the median, extreme overlaps diminished roughly in line with intuitive class dissimilarity, and some intuitively similar classes with little overlap (including vehicles 1 and vehicles 2) gained larger overlaps.
rows.note: The results are described qualitatively; the plotted overlap values are not transcribed.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.stage_stated: instruct; compared with a randomly initialized model
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap between neuron sets selected as important for different text subsets.
rows.measure: Intersection of selected neuron sets, divided by the size of one selected set
rows.value: Figure 4 only; the text says overlaps shifted toward the median, tending lower, and most extreme overlaps diminished roughly in line with intuitive subset dissimilarity. Similar subsets such as PubMed Abstracts, PubMed Central, and NIH ExPorter, or Ubuntu IRC and HackerNews, retained or gained overlap.
rows.note: The results are described qualitatively; the plotted overlap values are not transcribed.

rows.subject: ViT-Base-224
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned model, compared with a randomly initialized model
rows.operation_detail: Compared overall overlaps between class-selected neuron sets in trained and randomly initialized models.
rows.value: Figure 5 only; the text reports a definite correlation between random and pretrained overlaps, large shifts between them, and more tightly bounded overlaps in ViT than in Mistral.
rows.note: No numerical overlap values are given in the prose.

rows.subject: Mistral 7B instruct v0.2
rows.stage_stated: instruct; compared with a randomly initialized model
rows.operation_detail: Compared overall overlaps between subset-selected neuron sets in trained and randomly initialized models.
rows.value: Figure 5 only; the text reports a definite correlation between random and pretrained overlaps, large shifts between them, and overall lower overlaps in Mistral than in ViT.
rows.note: No numerical overlap values are given in the prose.
